controls_available: Six fixed room views navigated with visible TURN LEFT and TURN RIGHT buttons; navigation wraps around the view list.

Visible scene hotspots for revealing the digit clue, revealing the colour clue, revealing the separate reading-order card, collecting the handle and wire, collecting the two decoys, recovering the ward key, opening the door locks, and opening the final door.
Simplified inventory controls: select a visible tray object, then click a scene destination to use it or a second tray object to combine it.
A five-digit number dial and a six-colour sequence entry in the door lock panels; each has a visible submit control and each lock seizes after three wrong entries.
The combined hook chain: combine the handle and wire, use the hook on the grate for the ward key, then use the ward key on the door keyhole.
The door handle can complete the task only after the active digit, colour, and key wards are released.
autonomous_processes: None during gameplay: generated views, clues, hotspot geometry, inventory, lock answers, and flags remain unchanged until a user event.
After the final door action, the door receives a 0.8-second CSS transform transition; this is post-completion presentation after door_open and leaves no outcome-affecting action opportunity.
The result POST can asynchronously replace the page with pass or fresh-failure feedback, but that is administrative handling of the preceding action rather than autonomous task-state evolution.

grouped_control_modes.description: Direct scene-object actions, including clue discovery and the final door click.
Select two tray objects to combine them.
Select a tray object and click a visible scene target to use it.
Increment the number wheels and submit the digit ward.
Choose the colour sequence and submit the colour ward.

clause_i.reason: For a candidate grouped mode at the door's digit or colour entry, an observation-free q driven only by I_t cannot choose the correct seed-dependent five-digit or six-colour answer (or its independently sampled reading direction) across all occurrences. This is a static cross-view information requirement, not evidence of autonomous time evolution.

clause_ii.reason: At the later door lock action, the exact profile's w is bounded by observation_window_ms=0 and frames_per_observation=1; the current door-lock frame does not contain the digit, colour, or order clue previously exposed in other fixed views. Thus no bounded recent window supplies a common delayed-action policy for that lock-entry candidate. A clue visible in an earlier fixed view is cross-view memory, not a changing recent window.

clause_iii.reason: No legitimate grouped control mode has a useful action become unavailable or strictly less effective during an idle delay. The generator creates fixed per-seed clues and targets, and the browser changes flags, inventory, releases, wrong-entry counts, and completion only in direct event handlers. The only autonomous-looking transition is the final door CSS animation after door_open, when the outcome-affecting work is already complete; less remaining deadline or later administrative feedback would not satisfy the clause.

common_visible_process: No common visible autonomous process exists. Fixed-view clues and affordances persist while idle; the only visible autonomous transition is the post-completion door animation, which cannot degrade a remaining action opportunity.

pre_run.reason: There is no autonomous outcome phase to start after preparation. Every successful instance still requires outcome-affecting turn, reveal, combine/use, ward-submission, keyhole, and final door actions; the final door click sets completed and is not merely administrative. Therefore the required pre-run pattern is absent for the generated instances, and in any event it cannot override the mathematical No.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the six-view, three-ward, length-5 digit, length-6 colour, combined-hook, two-decoy, unmarked, cross-view-order configuration; simplified uses turn buttons and select-then-click inventory interaction; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame and a 240-second play allowance.

The generator derives a stable per-seed random challenge, samples fixed digit and colour clues and reading directions, and stores them as answers; no clock, timer, physics, or autonomous phase is generated.

The six view roles and all target rectangles are generated as fixed scene affordances; difficulty 5 adds the order drawer and two decoys while retaining synchronous object recipes and cross-view dependencies.
The browser renders fixed scenes, clue/order-card visibility, the number and colour controls, and simplified turn buttons from model state; no autonomous update loop is present.

Navigation, scene discoveries, combining, item use, ward submission, selection, and model state changes are all invoked by direct click handlers; open_door calls submit only after all wards are released, and render initializes a static state with no timer or frame callback.
The only time-duration styling found in the mechanic is the .8s transform transition for the vault door's is-open presentation; the terminal styling is applied after pass.

The authoritative replay starts from an initial static state, validates sequential user events and visible geometry, changes wards only on submitted actions, marks completion only on an explicit open_door scene event, and has no task-time evolution.
The verifier only loads the exported result and invokes the independent replay grader; it adds no autonomous outcome process.

The implementation solver performs the clue reveals, order discovery, hook construction/use, both lock submissions, keyhole use, and final door click as separate outcome-affecting actions; its private-state reads are not assumed available to a screenshot-only policy.
